one_liner: Mobile app that lets tenants pay rent by credit card, with the landlord paid by bank transfer through a payment aggregator partner.
sub_sector: Consumer payments - rent via credit card
ask: INR 1.8 Cr at INR 12 Cr post-money
business_model: Users pay a 1.8% fee on rent; ~0.9% goes to the payment aggregator, leaving ~0.9% net take rate.

founders.name: Sameer Qureshi
founders.background_claimed: Product manager at a fintech for 4 years; launched two payments features.

claims.text: Revenue is presented differently: deck shows 'INR 11 L revenue (1.8% fee)'; form says INR 11 L is gross and net revenue after the 0.9% paid to the payment partner is INR 5.5 L.
claims.note: Deck reports gross fees as revenue; true net take rate is ~0.9% of rent volume.

claims.text: Deck reports '1,900 users'; form clarifies 1,900 registered of whom 1,100 have paid at least once.
claims.note: Not a numeric contradiction, but the deck omits that ~42% of registered users have never paid.

claims.text: Competition differs across sources: deck says 'We have no direct competitors'; the form itself acknowledges banks and card networks have changed rent-payment rules before; the web shows several platforms offering card rent payments (RedGiraffe, PayZapp, NoBroker per W7; HDFC PayZapp's own rent page lists credit card as a method, W10).
claims.note: Deck claim is contradicted by independent sources; CRED, PhonePe and Paytm also offered the product until September 2025 (W2).

claims.text: Rent paid: INR 6.1 Cr across 2,400 payments since July 2026 (avg ~INR 25,400 per payment); monthly volume grew 0.4 -> 1.0 -> 1.9 -> 2.8 Cr (Jul-Oct).
Acquisition: mostly organic/word of mouth; small paid tests cost ~INR 120 per registered user; cost per paying user not measured.
claims.note: At a 58% registered-to-paid rate, ~INR 207 per paying user vs ~INR 229 net revenue per average payment (25,400 x 0.9%) - payback depends on repeat monthly use, which is not reported.

claims.text: RentRoute pays landlords through a single payment aggregator partner and states that a change in bank or card-network rules would hit it directly.
claims.note: Founders acknowledge the defining risk but give no mitigation plan.

claims.text: In February 2024 the RBI instructed Visa to suspend all transactions involving business payment solution providers (BPSPs), which routed card payments such as rent through fintechs.
RBI's Payment Aggregator Directions (September 2025) require a PA to aggregate funds only for merchants with whom it has a contractual relationship and prohibit PAs from running marketplaces.
claims.note: A landlord receiving card-funded rent must effectively be an onboarded merchant of the PA.

claims.text: CRED, PhonePe and Paytm halted credit-card rent payments in September 2025 following the RBI PA directions, because landlords were not onboarded with full merchant KYC.

By January 2026 some platforms (RedGiraffe, PayZapp, NoBroker) had restarted or continued card rent payments with stricter verification - PAN of both payer and payee plus rent agreement documents; PhonePe stayed out.
claims.note: Shows a compliant route may exist, but with KYC friction RentRoute does not describe (deck: 'Enter your landlord's bank details once').

claims.text: Whether RentRoute's flow complies with the 2025 PA directions (landlord onboarded as the PA's merchant with KYC) is not established by the application.
claims.note: Relevant to gate G2 (exists only if the rules are favourable): the business launched in July 2026, after the rules that shut the incumbents' version.

claims.text: Planned issuer referral income ('Referral income from card issuers is coming') is unsupported in the application.

Founders: Sameer Qureshi (CEO) claims 4 years as a fintech product manager who launched two payments features; Divya Menon (Growth) claims 5 years in consumer marketing. Engineering is outsourced to contract developers. Sameer full-time since June 2026, Divya since August 2026.
claims.note: No in-house engineering or compliance/payments-regulation lead on the team.

claims.text: Founder LinkedIn links are placeholders (*-example) and the website is a .example domain; no independent footprint for founders or company found.
Market sizing is top-down: INR 1.5 lakh Cr annual urban rent, 'capturing just 1%' = INR 1,500 Cr volume.
12-month target INR 20 Cr monthly rent volume (~7x October); 55% of the raise goes to marketing.
Raising INR 1.8 Cr at INR 12 Cr post-money; no outside investors; founders have put in INR 18 L and own 100%.
Sector as selected (Fintech) matches the business: a consumer payments app (rent via credit card).
Founders frame rent as a large, underserved payment category and the problem as landlords not accepting cards.

research_notes: Founder and company searches returned nothing (placeholder links). Business Standard article on the September 2025 shutdown returned 403; Inc42, Entrackr and IndiaCorpLaw used instead. Search snippets also reported HDFC Bank's June 2024 1% fee on card rent payments and ICICI/SBI Card removing rewards on rent, but no page with a verbatim quote was retrieved for these, so they are not cited as sources. Whalesbook (Jan 2026) is a lesser-known outlet; its report that some platforms resumed rent payments should be confirmed.
